pairs.why: The saddles are nearly the same, but A's hay is drawn in broader, smoother clumps, while B's fine, busy straw is the 'too texture-y' look the lessons mark down.
Same saddle in both; A's chunkier, softer hay matches the smooth-but-not-ultra-smooth finish of the real cards better than B's fine straw strands.
A keeps the hay in bold, simple clumps on a clean blue ground, while B's hay has finer, busier texture.
A's hay is broader and smoother, while B's finely stranded straw reads as more texture-heavy than the real cards.
Both are near-identical; A's hay is chunkier and less finely detailed, which is closer to the real cards' simplified surfaces.
A's simpler, smoother hay clumps fit the real cards better than B's dense fine strands; the saddles themselves are equivalent.
A's cactus is smoother and simpler, with soft ribs like the real cards' toy-like surfaces, while B adds more ribbing, spine dots and a leaf collar.
Very close call; B's cactus is slightly cleaner and smoother, while A adds a leaf collar and a little more surface detail, but both share the same glossy toy finish.
